name: High-cardinality group-by
why: Top customers by error volume across 50k distinct customer_id values. This is where a columnar store and an inverted index diverge most, and the dimension vendor benchmarks usually omit. Both sides run the same question: filter to ERROR, group by a 50k-cardinality attribute, take the top 20. Against PulseTrace this reaches Quickwit as a filtered terms aggregation; the rows are counted in the index and only the 20 buckets travel.

body.sql: SELECT `metadata.customer_id`, count(*) AS n FROM logs WHERE level = 'ERROR' GROUP BY `metadata.customer_id` ORDER BY n DESC LIMIT 20

query.sql: SELECT customer_id, count(*) AS n FROM bench_logs WHERE level = 'ERROR' GROUP BY customer_id ORDER BY n DESC LIMIT 20
